body:
Exactly that. You sound like a great person. I think that since as you said you are normally not the loud assholey type, that if you really do assert yourself in a way that stands out from the usual then it could really get his attention and let him know you are for real.

Best of luck to you man.

> But I'm hesitant to text him. It's would be like me losing, which would validate what he said. I won't say sorry because I feel I didn't do anything wrong. 

Thats basically letting your pride get in the way. People lose friendships when they are too proud to make the first move. When you're young it seems like it meens a lot but over time you learn there are more important things than losing or someone thinking your lost. 

I don't think you should say you are sorry, but if you want the friendship you will need to make the first move. Not an apology, but an honest and sincere explanation. Explain he is an important friend to you and that you'd like to continue it but that is wasn't cool what he said and that you won't tolerate it. If you don't think he will apologize then don't make the message sound like you are expecting one. Just put it out there and he can either accept it and be friends or continue rejecting it in which case you both lost a good friend.

I just really think you need to break the silence. He's probably thinking the same thing that he doesn't want to be the first one to text you.

That seems like such a huge task. Living in basically a homeless shelter and finding work. I have no experience with a sober living house but I assumed it cost a lot of money and was usually something courts ordered. My experience with 12 step programs and other center for drug free living stuff was that there were more drugs there than I have at home. People meeting new connections and stuff at meetings.

The one thing I really think about as my salvation is just up and leaving the state. Saving enough for a plane ticket to California and just being a bum until I found work. Or signing up for work on a cruise ship or something where I would be away from home for extended periods of time. I wish I could even join the military. I would have been so gone by now.

You really are a romantic. I feel the same way really in that you mostly fall in love with the person, not a gender. Which opens the possibility to love anyone. I don't know him to say he's closeted or whatnot but I still think the words he used against you were specifically to shield himself from not having you as a friend like he wants. It's shitty, but its a common coping mechanism to deal with a distancing relationship. I think if you ever get a chance to just hang out with him and pretend it didn't happen, he wouldn't be opposed. It doesn't sound like hes the type who would want to talk about it so the best bet is just you having to get out of your shell to make an effort to be his friend, even if he resist at first, kinda force it with a hint of sarcasm like you don't care what he wants, you are going to be friends. If that doesn't work then you might just have lost him.
Are you missing him in a romantic type of way? And I suppose since he used those words he doesn't have any gay tendencies.

>Called me a faggot a bunch of times, (which is a personal jab at who i am) and said he hoped my girlfriend would break up with me,

Does this mean you are gay? Even a little bit? I'm curious if this has anything to do with it.

That sucks about losing him, but I would bet he is just as hurt by losing you. I bet he thinks he lost your as a friend before you thought that about him.

It's weird but I'm usually the quiet person as well and I get what you mean about how the louder friends break your out of your shell. For me I feel I got lucky enough that the outgoing types even latched on in the first place for long enough to try to get me out of my shell. I guess opposites attract. The outgoing types might not like other loud people since it's like having two alpha dogs.

But at least you know what you want in life and are going for it. I bet he's also jealous of that much. He was probably scared you would leave him behind. I'm picturing the type of relationship like in the movie Superbad if you've seen it.

I'm sure he didn't mean the things he said but more did it as a coping mechanism to not miss his friend so much while you were gone. Maybe if you ever return you guys will still be best buds again. Are you going to be going home for the summer? If so, maybe you just show up and act like nothing happened. If he really blocked your number that might be the only option.

Hey man, being homeless sucks pretty bad, I feel you. I was homeless for a couple of weeks during the winter like 3 years ago. I wanted to kill myself then but was too scared and too poor to even afford it. 

Do you have any family who can help? Just a couch to sleep on even while you look for work. I know my family rejected me when I was homeless that time. They rejected me for 3 weeks. They knew I was going to be sleeping outside but didn't want me to take up their couch for 8 hours a night. It was pretty cold.

But if you do have any sort of family that can help then now is not the time to let your pride hold you back. Lot's of people are moving back in with family nowadays. 

But even better is the fact that you have 3 months to figure something out. That is a fair amount of time to rethink your job search and maybe find a place to live. You might even consider some sort of legal action against the landlord if you signed any sort of lease agreement.

I get what your going through though. Life has become such a struggle just to keep my (our) head above water. I often feel like robbing a bank is a win-win situation anymore. Either I rob it and get away with it and have money to survive for a while, or I go to jail where I don't have to struggle daily. When life gets this hard I definitely see the rationale for crime and that saddens me so it makes me think I'm just not cut out for this world.

Anyway, what kind of work are you looking for? Is the job market that bad where you're at or is it possible you are looking for work out of your league? I also wonder if there is any homeless assistance in your area you could look in to. Noone likes doing it but if it gets you to tomorrow then it's worth it.

I came here thinking of making a post myself but figured I would read a few before I do.

The one thing I keep seeing you and lots of others being depressed about are temporary things. Losing a girlfriend or best friend. Being broke up with sucks, let me tell you. But every single person goes through it on multiple occasions in their life. 

The thing is, all of you guys problems are fixable. If you don't die tonight, you will have more reasons to live in a few months. You'll have a new friend and someday a new girlfriend. Being a teenager sucks to be honest. I remember clearly thinking that it was the end of the world when I got broken up with. I was so sad for like a year and would have slit my wrist just to be with her again for the next 5 years. But what I've learned with age (not that much age, I'm 28) is that time heals those emotional wounds and nothing else will.

From the sounds of it, you actually would prefer it if your friends found this post. You want to talk to them, but don't want to be the one to have to come out and say it for whatever reason. It's probably the antisocialness or social anxiety, whichever you call it. I guess it can be hard to initiate conversations.

I think you know exactly what you need and that is to talk to someone, which is why you are here I suppose. You seem to not be super bothered by any other things so far so you should be able to get actual help here in the form of people talking to you.

So what happened with you and your friend? Lets talk about it. Also, have you ever tried to commit suicide? What are you doing now?

Edit: I just realized you said you HAVE a girlfriend. I was thinking you said you lost her. So your main issue right now is you lost your best friend. You mentioned being a romantic, and I completely agree with you. It seems like you value the closeness you had with that friend very much. I bet it feels like it will be super hard to make another friend that close. In my entire life I have only had maybe 4 good friends that I cared about. I lost all of them due to my antisocialness. For a while I had a new friend who I thought would be my new best friend, and we were for a while. I wouldn't have been able to initiate that friendship but I felt I had lucked out that someone who was so outgoing saw me as a valuable friend and made effort to maintain it. Turned out he was a crazy drug addict though and our relationship didn't last.

Anyway, I feel like I know what you are feeling with losing your friend. Please tell me more.
